*Paṇṇattivārauddesa* is a section belonging to the *Yamaka*, the sixth book of the Theravāda *Abhidhammapiṭaka* [SuttaCentral]. As designated by its title, the text constitutes the summary matrix or uddesa for the *Paṇṇattivāra* ("Section on Designations") within the fifth chapter of the *Yamaka* (the *Saccayamaka*), laying down the foundational categories and phrasing subsequently analyzed in detail [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral registers one translation of the text in one language [SuttaCentral].

Computational text-reuse data indicates substantial shared material with other canonical and post-canonical Pali literature, comprising 529 matches across 14 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Unsurprisingly, its closest structural partner is its direct expository sequel, the *Paṇṇattivāraniddesa* (Ya 5.1.2), alongside the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi* [DharmaNexus]. Due to its focus on the four noble truths, it shares recurring formulas with core truth expositions, notably the *Sacca Saṁyutta* (SN 56), the *Saccakathā* of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 2.2), and the *Saccavibhaṅga* (Vb 4), as well as other *Yamaka* subsections (*Uppādavāra*, *Nirodhavāra*, and *Uppādanirodhavāra*) and the *Dasuttara Sutta* (DN 34) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language machine alignments identified by DharmaNexus also match segments with Tibetan translations of the *Brahmaviśeṣacintiparipṛcchā-sūtra* (D0160) and the *Aṣṭādaśasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā* (D0010-3), though these represent automated computational reuses rather than established historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
